title: Introducing artifacts for legal work
summary: Ready-to-use interactive artifacts such as trackers and dashboards are now available for legal teams, including a legal gallery for cite-checking, contract vs. standard terms, regulatory tracking, and side-by-side review. The release includes nine access-to-justice artifacts and launches the Legal Ambassadors Program, with artifacts shareable internally and externally under privacy and ethical-wall settings. Outputs link to their sources so lawyers can verify them.

title: New agents and products for security, productivity, and creative work on Claude Marketplace
summary: Claude Marketplace adds new partner listings, bringing the total to over 25 partner agents and products. Partners span security (Chainguard, Checkmarx, Cyera, Rubrik, Tanium), dev infrastructure (Datadog, Netlify), marketing and creative (AirOps, Runway, Webflow), and productivity (Asana, Glean, monday, Zoom). Eligible enterprises can apply committed Anthropic spend to partner products, and builders can apply to join the marketplace.

title: IDC brings Quanta into Claude and adopts Claude across the company
summary: The IDC Quanta platform is now available in Claude as a connector, drawing answers from IDC forecasts, market data, and research with citations. Customers can use it to produce competitor briefs, vendor shortlists, and budget comparisons in minutes. IDC also rolled Claude out internally, cutting code review time from 5 days to about 30 minutes.

title: Claude for Financial Advisors
summary: Connectors and workflow skills help financial advisors with research, meeting prep, and documentation, connecting to custodians such as Schwab, Addepar, and BlackRock along with CRMs and planning tools. Skills cover meeting prep and notes, rebalance review, estate and tax briefs, and SEC Marketing Rule checks, with approval required for critical tasks so the advisor stays in control. It is available now as a Cowork plugin, and Enterprise is recommended for audit logs.

title: Smart reports, surveys, and pooled group budgets for Claude Enterprise
summary: Three Claude Enterprise features are now generally available: smart reports, in-app surveys, and pooled group budgets. Smart reports analyze sampled team transcripts for workstreams, spend, deliverables, friction, and skill recommendations, while surveys gather customizable, exportable team feedback. Pooled group budgets add a shared monthly limit with member guardrails and admin threshold alerts, and these features are meant for adoption planning rather than individual performance reviews.

title: Introducing Personal Finance in Claude
summary: Personal Finance connects bank and card accounts so users can ask plain-language questions about their money, in beta for Pro, Max, and Ultra plans in the US. It is read-only and cannot move or invest money, and accounts link via Plaid so Claude never sees the bank password; it can categorize spending, flag unusual charges, and explain terms. Hub conversations are not used for model training, accounts can be unlinked anytime, and there are no ads or sponsored recommendations.
